title: Chronicle Tales — I got tired of AI story games forgetting everything
author: Maximum_Maximum9555
selftext:
I’ve played a few AI story games. They’re fun for a while, and then the bartender suddenly doesn’t know you anymore, the knife you picked up has vanished, and the plot seems to have developed amnesia.

I got annoyed enough that I decided to try building one myself.

Chronicle Tales is an AI text adventure where I’m trying to make the world actually remember what happens. Characters, places, objects, little details and things you’ve done should persist and matter later.

It’s still in beta, and it definitely isn’t perfect. Sometimes it still forgets things. That’s actually the part I’m most interested in improving.

And yes, the game is built around AI. The actual storytelling and gameplay are AI-driven, and AI is naturally used throughout development as well.

But I’m also experimenting with using AI for something slightly different: as a kind of **housekeeper for the game world**.

Instead of throwing the entire story history at the model every time, the game extracts and maintains structured information about characters, locations, objects, relationships and other pieces of lore. AI helps decide what information is important, update the lore, and keep the world state organized.

The goal is basically to give the AI a memory it can actually work with, rather than just hoping it remembers everything from a giant conversation history.

It’s still very much an experiment.

If anyone enjoys this kind of game and wants to poke holes in it, I’d genuinely appreciate some playtesting:

[http://chronicletales.com/](http://chronicletales.com/)

If you find something the game forgets or gets wrong, there’s a report button in-game.
